o1.biggest_strength: It catches and acts on every signal in the data: the Monsoon Dark gap gets its own named track, the courier problem gates the ex-subscriber win-back, and the at-risk 46-90 day group is worked first with no discount.
o1.biggest_mistake: The message drafts rely on merge fields with template syntax ('{{ last_coffee | default: "your coffee" }}') that will need cleaning before a non-technical team can paste them into a real ESP, and the 46-90 day group is placed first while it is technically 'at risk' rather than 'lapsed', which could confuse a reader expecting a purely lapsed audience.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Plain-text merge fields with a one-line note on what each field pulls, so the team can load the drafts into their email tool without touching the code.

o2.biggest_strength: The offer logic is immediately usable and the reasoning about why a 10% discount costs ₹115 of a ₹557 order is clear enough for a non-expert to follow and defend to a founder.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 12-month gross profit projection double-counts value by assuming each won-back buyer places two orders (worth ₹999) while the table is presented as the return from the programme, and the assumed lift rates are not tested against a break-even threshold the way the brief asked.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Show the break-even lift rate per group (the minimum lift needed to cover discounts and message costs) and drop the invented multi-order value assumption so the projection is conservative and defensible.

reason: Output 1 reads like it was written by someone who knows the store: it names the discontinued blend, gates the ex-subscriber track on the delivery fix, holds out 10% everywhere and builds gross profit from ₹557 per order, while Output 2 is solid but pads its projection with multi-order assumptions and never gives a break-even lift rate.
